aiOverview.content: The Artemis II moon mission is designed to last approximately 10 days, during which a four-person crew will orbit the Moon and return to Earth. Launched on April 1, 2026, the mission features a "free-return" trajectory, allowing the Orion spacecraft to loop around the Moon and return without major propulsion maneuvers, with a final splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. Key Mission Timeline (Approximate): Launch & Earth Orbit (Day 1): The crew performs system checks and initial orbital maneuvers. Trans-Lunar Injection (Day 2): Orion fires engines to leave Earth orbit for the Moon. Deep Space Travel (Days 3-5): Trajectory adjustments and manual flying tests are conducted. Lunar Flyby (Day 6): The crew flies 4,000–6,000 miles from the Moon's far side, entering the deepest point of their mission. Return Trip (Days 7-9): The spacecraft travels back to Earth, including testing of radiation protection. Reentry (Day 10): Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, as described in.
